text:
Caroline: Quick sync — proposing a concise span naming + attribute set for inference traces. Goal: make it easy to filter by model, tokens, cache hits, routing policy, and backend variant. Ping @Sasha @Matt for API/console implications.

Sasha: +1. Can you sketch the opname and the minimal attribute set? we should keep it small for retention and cost.

Caroline: Draft idea: operation name = "redwood.inference.request" (generic) and then use attributes to distinguish phase/step: "span.role": ["ingress", "batcher", "executor"] so common tooling can group by role.

Matt: I like a single opname for aggregation. But add a convention for short human tag for quick queries, e.g. "span.short": "infer/model-name" or use "resource.service.name"?

Omar: small nit: prefer "service.name" for exporter compatibility. Example keys we should standardize: model.name, model.revision, model.quantized, tokens.prompt, tokens.completion, tokens.total, kv_cache.hit (bool), routing.policy, backend.machine_type.

Caroline: Agreed. Proposed canonical attribute set (minimal + optional):
- model.name (required)
- model.revision (optional)
- model.variant (optional, e.g., fp16-q4_0)
- model.quantized = true|false (optional)
- tokens.prompt (int)
- tokens.completion (int)
- tokens.total (int)
- kv_cache.hit = true|false
- routing.policy = {latency|cost|regional|tiered} (string)
- backend.variant (string)
- customer.id (optional, for sampling/retention)

Sasha: Two operational asks: 1) ensure token counts are integers (no floats), 2) kv_cache attribute should include source when true (kv_cache.source = "prefix"|"external"). Also we should avoid embedding full prompts in spans.

Matt: For span.name alternatives: I tested two patterns in logs: 
1) "redwood.inference.request" + span.role attr
2) "redwood.inference/<model.name>" as opname
Pattern 1 gives better cardinality control. prefer that.

Omar: exporter side — we need to map these attrs to Jaeger/OTLP resource/attributes and reserve a schema version attr: telemetry.schema = "rlm.v1" so we can evolve. Also add sampling hint: telemetry.sample_rate (0-1).

InfraBot: deploy-batch: scheduled job will add span processors to strip sensitive attrs and cap string lengths >256. Config snippet: 
```yaml
processors:
  - attribute/limit: max_length=256
  - sampling: parentbased=traceIdRateLimit
```

Caroline: retention and sampling idea: default traces retention 30d for infra metrics, but for customer-tier=enterprise we keep 90d. Use customer.id to drive per-tenant retention in pipeline. Also keep only aggregated token histograms longer-term instead of full traces.

Sasha: UX/console: expose quick filters for model.name and kv_cache.hit so SREs can pivot. For rollout UX (canary) we should add span.attr rollout.bucket and rollout.variant so traces can be sliced by canary group.

Matt: security: confirm we never set prompt content as an attribute or resource. If someone requests tracing prompt-level debugging, require an explicit opt-in and retention guardrails.

Caroline: Action items: 1) Sasha => mockup console filters and add rollout filter; 2) Omar => OTLP to Jaeger mapping + add telemetry.schema attr; 3) Matt => add docs PR with canonical keys + examples; 4) Infra => add processor to cap attr lengths and drop prompt. I'll follow up with a compact JSON example of a span.

Omar: one more: consider adding metric export of token counts per-model to avoid heavy trace queries. we can aggregate tokens as metrics with labels {model.name, quantized}.

Caroline: noted. Thanks all :thumbsup:
